facts.detail: Ofcom first published the codes-of-practice page on 28 April 2010.
The page was last updated on 16 July 2025.
Updated broadband-speed codes apply to purchases from 21 December 2022.
Section 52 of the Communications Act requires complaint and dispute procedures.
General Condition C4 governs complaint handling and dispute resolution.
GC C4.2 requires providers to follow the Ofcom Approved Complaints Code.
GC C4.3 requires membership of and compliance with an approved ADR scheme.
Formal non-compliance can attract a penalty up to ten percent of turnover.
Automatic compensation covers delayed repairs, missed appointments and delayed service starts.
The 2022 speed-code update aligned exit rights with revised General Conditions implemented on 17 June 2022.

guard_streams.write_limit: Annual national and regional infrastructure reports are aggregate snapshots and cannot establish selected-parcel orderability or measured speed without an exact current join.

facts.detail: Ofcom published Connected Nations 2025 on 19 November 2025.
Connected Nations is Ofcom's annual communications-infrastructure report.
The report covers availability of broadband services in the UK.
The report also covers availability of mobile services.
The report includes progress in fixed full-fibre rollout.
The report includes progress in mobile 5G rollout.
Ofcom published a UK main report.
Separate reports were published for each UK nation.
An interactive report provides area and service views.
Published data downloads support year-on-year infrastructure comparisons.
